title: Exact extension adjoint for localized restriction
statement: For a sheaf of rings R on a Grothendieck site and an object U, assuming localized restriction preserves zero morphisms, there exists a functor G from localized module sheaves to module sheaves preserving finite limits and finite colimits and left adjoint to restriction.

proof.text: Construct the direct-sum presheaf over arrows V → U, with scalar action on each summand and restrictions into the composite-arrow summand. Sheafify it to obtain an additive functor G. A map from the localized sheaf to restriction gives a map from each summand, and conversely precomposition with each summand inclusion recovers such a map. These operations are inverse and natural, so module sheafification gives the adjunction. Monomorphisms are sectionwise injections, direct sums preserve injections, and exact module sheafification preserves monomorphisms by lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact. The additive left adjoint G is right exact and preserves monomorphisms, hence exact; it preserves kernels and finite biproducts, hence finite limits, and its adjunction gives finite colimits.

theorem localized_restriction_extension_exists
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    (hzero : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U).PreservesZeroMorphisms) :
    ∃ (G : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (R.over U) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max u v} R),
      PreservesFiniteLimits G ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits G ∧
      Nonempty (G ⊣ SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R U)
